title: Cells and organisation: data question set (20 marks)
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Review of Key Stage 3 and working scientifically (9C)
source: Written for science/y9 lesson 50 (Cells data question set (20 marks) and mark scheme (portal))
intro: Answer every question. Show working and units for calculations. Mark it with the mark scheme.

questions.q: Name the parts of a plant cell that are not found in an animal cell.
questions.a: Cell wall, chloroplasts, permanent vacuole (1 each)

questions.q: Give the function of the nucleus and of the mitochondria.
questions.a: Nucleus: controls the cell and holds genetic material; mitochondria: where respiration releases energy

questions.q: An image of a cell is 40 mm long. The magnification is × 200. Calculate the real size.
A cell is 0.05 mm long and its image is 25 mm. Calculate the magnification.
Put in order of size, smallest first: organ, system, cell, tissue.
Explain how a root hair cell is adapted to its job.
questions.a: Long, thin extension gives a large surface area (1) to absorb water and mineral ions quickly (1)

questions.q: Explain why palisade cells have many chloroplasts.
questions.a: Chloroplasts absorb light (1) for photosynthesis, so more chloroplasts means more photosynthesis (1)

questions.q: Explain two ways red blood cells are adapted to carry oxygen.
questions.a: No nucleus, so more room for haemoglobin (1); biconcave shape gives a large surface area (1); flexible to fit through capillaries (1)

questions.q: A student counts 12 cells across a field of view 1.2 mm wide. Estimate the width of one cell in micrometres.
